report.target_evidence: Research.FloatingPoint.Horner.forward_error directly asserts the requested universal forward-error bound about the three explicitly defined recursions. Both directions preserve the model assumptions, input domains, exact recurrence, two-rounding algorithm, and prescribed envelope. No additional conclusion or formal bridge is needed.

requirements.requirement: Prove the full forward-error theorem for every model, coefficient list, and real evaluation point.
requirements.evidence: The explicit target Research.FloatingPoint.Horner.forward_error asserts the full inequality for every model m, every finite real list c including [], and every real x. It is the final theorem itself, with no missing composition of supporting lemmas.

requirements.requirement: Use the exact Horner recursion with zero for the empty list and coefficients in increasing degree order.
requirements.evidence: Construction P defines P([],x)=0 and P(a::t,x)=a+x P(t,x) using exact real operations. It explicitly identifies the head as the constant coefficient and the list as coefficients in increasing degree order.

requirements.requirement: Evaluate each cons step using a rounded multiplication of x and the rounded tail, then a rounded addition of the coefficient.
requirements.evidence: Construction Q defines Q(m,[],x)=0 and Q(m,a::t,x)=r(a+r(x Q(m,t,x))), with r=round(m). This rounds the product with the rounded tail and then the addition, twice per element including the last.

requirements.requirement: Define the stated error envelope using exact values and u, with the requested recurrence and base case.
requirements.evidence: Construction E defines E([],x,u)=0 and E(a::t,x,u)=u|a+x v|+(1+u)(u|x v|+(1+u)|x|e), where v=P(t,x) and e=E(t,x,u). This is exactly the requested recurrence, using only exact tail values and the listed inputs.

requirements.requirement: Bound the absolute difference of the supplied rounded and exact evaluators by the supplied envelope.
requirements.evidence: The target explicitly identifies P, Q, E with the supplied recursions and asserts |Q(m,c,x)-P(c,x)|<=E(c,x,u(m)). The list, argument, rounding model, and its parameter are linked exactly as requested.

requirements.requirement: Use the supplied relative-error model without additional smallness, sign, nonzero, or exact-arithmetic premises.
requirements.evidence: The model supplies only u>=0 and, for every real z, a delta with |delta|<=u and round(z)=z(1+delta). The target imposes no extra hypotheses or upper bound on u; all real coefficients and arguments are covered. Exact real reference operations do not assume that rounding is exact.

requirements.requirement: Evaluate each cons step using a rounded multiplication of x and the rounded tail, then a rounded addition of the coefficient.
requirements.evidence: Research/Submission.lean:24-26 defines Q model [] x = 0 and Q model (a :: tail) x = model.round (a + model.round (x * Q model tail x)). This performs exactly the prescribed rounded product followed by rounded addition at each cons step; lines 42-45 expose the same equations.

requirements.requirement: Define the stated error envelope using exact values and u, with the requested recurrence and base case.
requirements.evidence: Research/Submission.lean:30-35 defines E with empty value 0 and cons value u * |a + x * v| + (1 + u) * (u * |x * v| + (1 + u) * |x| * e), where v = P tail x and e = E tail x u. It uses only exact P, coefficients, x, and u; lines 47-52 confirm the recurrence.

requirements.requirement: Bound the absolute difference of the supplied rounded and exact evaluators by the supplied envelope.
requirements.evidence: Research/Submission.lean:82 directly bounds |Q model coefficients x - P coefficients x| by E coefficients x model.u. Lines 87-102 bound the rounded product using the induction hypothesis; lines 103-114 unfold the supplied P, Q, and E and apply the rounded-addition estimate to obtain that exact envelope.

requirements.evidence: Research/Common/FloatingPoint/Model.lean:15-19 supplies only u, u_nonneg, round, and the universal relative rounding law. Research/Submission.lean:81-82 adds no hypotheses beyond model, list, and real x. Lines 54-76 derive rounding estimates from round_spec and u_nonneg; line 83 derives nonnegativity of 1 + u.
